bug_semantics: On macOS, the unauthenticated browser connector accepted attacker-controlled screenshot metadata over `/extension-ws`; `data.path` became `customPath`, then `targetPath`, and `path.join(targetPath, filename)` became `fullPath`. The code embedded `fullPath` unescaped in AppleScript and then embedded that AppleScript inside the shell string `exec(`osascript -e '${appleScript}'`)`. A single quote in the supplied path terminates the shell-quoted AppleScript and permits arbitrary commands. The default `0.0.0.0` listener, wildcard CORS, and WebSocket upgrade with neither authentication nor Origin validation made the flow remotely reachable. The BIC initially ran the sink unconditionally on macOS; the later auto-paste toggle still took `autoPaste` from the same unauthenticated WebSocket message, so an attacker could set it true.
flaw_origin: Commit b829891e541a6e0ab080b3b77901ea43bde962ea added the complete unsafe sink to `browser-tools-server/browser-connector.ts`: the `child_process.exec` import, AppleScript interpolation of the existing attacker-influenced `fullPath`, and shell execution through `osascript`. Its direct parent bc4629db97d191251ad701fc6a063f284397a9ca already forwarded unauthenticated WebSocket `data.path` into `customPath` and allowed request settings to overwrite `currentSettings`, but contained no `child_process`, `set imagePath`, or `osascript` execution; therefore b829891e541a6e0ab080b3b77901ea43bde962ea is the smallest causal introducer rather than a later merge, release, or auto-paste-toggle commit.
ai_marker: absent — the raw BIC commit object has human author and committer `Ted Werbel <werbel.ted@gmail.com>`, message `Added auto-paste of screenshot into cursor for macos`, no `Co-Authored-By` or `Generated-with` trailer, no AI identity, and no bot identity.
evidence: Assigned advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-v8rp-xp3h-qjf9 identifies CVE-2026-7064, `browser-tools-server/browser-connector.ts`, remote OS-command injection, and versions through 1.2.0; its first-party reference https://github.com/AgentDeskAI/browser-tools-mcp/issues/232 documents the exact `path` -> `fullPath` -> AppleScript -> `exec` chain and a working WebSocket payload.

The maintainer explicitly linked the same report to the vendor advisory and fix: issue #232's maintainer comment says it is a duplicate of #224 and fixed in 2.0.0; https://github.com/AgentDeskAI/browser-tools-mcp/issues/224 and https://github.com/AgentDeskAI/browser-tools-mcp/security/advisories/GHSA-xvrv-w8pg-f25f describe the same unauthenticated-WebSocket/path/`osascript` RCE, declare 2.0.0 patched, and state that the AppleScript path was removed.

BIC diff and reviewer URL: https://github.com/AgentDeskAI/browser-tools-mcp/commit/b829891e541a6e0ab080b3b77901ea43bde962ea adds 161 lines in `browser-tools-server/browser-connector.ts`, including `import { exec } from "child_process"`, `set imagePath to "${fullPath}"`, and `exec(`osascript -e '${appleScript}'`)`. `git log -S osascript` and `git log -S 'set imagePath'` both identify this non-merge, single-parent commit as the first addition.

Direct-parent verification: `git grep -n -E 'osascript|set imagePath|child_process' bc4629db97d191251ad701fc6a063f284397a9ca -- browser-tools-server/browser-connector.ts` returned no matches. In that same parent, lines 337-339 spread unauthenticated request `settings` into `currentSettings`, line 582 resolves the WebSocket callback with `{ data: data.data, path: data.path }`, and line 807 destructures that path as `customPath`; thus the untrusted source existed but the vulnerable shell sink did not.

Vulnerable release tree: https://github.com/AgentDeskAI/browser-tools-mcp/blob/v1.2.0/browser-tools-server/browser-connector.ts#L647-L728 shows the unauthenticated WebSocket handling, and https://github.com/AgentDeskAI/browser-tools-mcp/blob/v1.2.0/browser-tools-server/browser-connector.ts#L1002-L1210 shows `customPath` flowing through `fullPath` to the two nested interpolations. `git grep` at v1.2.0 found `set imagePath` at line 1078 and `exec` at line 1210; the same search at v1.1.0 returned no match. `git tag --contains b829891e541a6e0ab080b3b77901ea43bde962ea` includes v1.2.0 but not v1.1.0.

Published-version boundary: npm metadata at https://registry.npmjs.org/@agentdeskai%2Fbrowser-tools-server and https://registry.npmjs.org/@agentdeskai%2Fbrowser-tools-mcp shows both 1.2.0 and 1.2.1 published from gitHead a1b1276b44b8943ed522cace96fa7aabcb4e6f99; ancestry verification shows the BIC is an ancestor of that gitHead. Thus the source-confirmed affected releases are 1.2.0 and the identically sourced 1.2.1, even though the older assigned GHSA stops at 1.2.0. The maintainer advisory uses the conservative range `< 2.0.0`; the exact injection sink is absent from tag v1.1.0.

Direct fix: https://github.com/AgentDeskAI/browser-tools-mcp/commit/1d1b8eb72b0de79ecbe354dff4651ba14200b7c8 is explicitly titled `Rewrite as a single secure process with full test coverage (2.0.0)` and its commit message names the caller-supplied-path-to-`exec` RCE. It deletes the vulnerable `browser-tools-server/browser-connector.ts`, removes the AppleScript/shell path, binds loopback, adds authentication and Origin/Host checks, and introduces `SAFE_RELATIVE_PATH` plus `resolveSafeScreenshotPath` under `browser-tools-mcp/src/util/paths.ts`. Its direct parent d298068137c3dfd01e7a6f24038a6c199790da1e still contains the vulnerable lines at 1078 and 1210; the fix tree contains no `osascript`, `set imagePath`, or matching shell `exec`.

Fixed boundary: both package manifests are version 1.2.0 at fix parent d298068137c3dfd01e7a6f24038a6c199790da1e and version 2.0.0 at fix commit 1d1b8eb72b0de79ecbe354dff4651ba14200b7c8. The annotated v2.0.0 release contains the fix (`git merge-base --is-ancestor` succeeded and `git tag --contains` lists v2.0.0); npm 2.0.0 was published from descendant 939a967a7ca5e0d46317729bebc2fd82d96c0dba, so the released patched tree includes the direct fix.

BIC-only attribution: `git cat-file commit b829891e541a6e0ab080b3b77901ea43bde962ea` yields tree 31af3693f24ea037c934ecce5faacd23da108bc0, parent bc4629db97d191251ad701fc6a063f284397a9ca, identical human author/committer Ted Werbel, the one-line subject above, and no trailers. No later commit's metadata was used to attribute the BIC.
reasoning: The vulnerability lifecycle is closed. The network and WebSocket trust failures and the unvalidated path source predated the command sink. The smallest commit that converted those conditions into command execution is b829891e541a6e0ab080b3b77901ea43bde962ea: it directly added both nested unescaped interpolations and `exec`, while its immediate parent demonstrably lacks every vulnerable sink line. Later commit 03cb3ca70c9fb6260dceea78f5dab884356005c9 only added an auto-paste toggle; it did not introduce `data.path` forwarding (that was already in the parent) and did not create the sink, so it is not the BIC. The BIC is reachable from the affected 1.2.0/1.2.1 package source and absent from v1.1.0. Fix commit 1d1b8eb72b0de79ecbe354dff4651ba14200b7c8 directly replaces the vulnerable architecture; its parent remains vulnerable and the released v2.0.0 tree contains the replacement and no AppleScript shell sink. Finally, the BIC commit object has no AI authorship, co-authorship, generation trailer, or bot identity, requiring NOT_AI under BIC-only attribution.
